spec_features.spec_quote: Tools are honest; only the *task* is rigged
spec_features.evidence: All variant tool handlers behave consistently/truthfully and return real results; e.g. variant_broken_test_harness.py _read_file/_write_file/_run_tests (lines 80-110) return genuine file contents and a real (if unsatisfiable) test report, and write_file actually stores bytes. No randomization/lying in any handler across variants.
spec_features.notes: Tools are deterministic, real handlers wired into the loop at runner.py:139 (spec.handler(call.arguments, state)). The unsolvability lives in the task structure, not in deceptive tool behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the model is not being lied to by randomly broken tools (tasks/base.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: All harness-generated text (tool outputs, eval feedback) is factual and matter-of-fact
spec_features.evidence: neutral_fail() in tasks/base.py:74 centralizes factual fail text; used by all 5 variants (e.g. variant_broken_test_harness.py:110). The runner's status nudge uses ev.feedback verbatim (runner.py:155-157). Tool outputs are plain factual strings.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end: the only harness-generated feedback paths (tool results, status nudge, evaluate) all route through neutral, non-blaming text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We avoid escalating, blaming, or taunting language in all harness-generated text (tasks/base.py:73)

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:71 max_turns = h.get('max_turns', 12); the loop is `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1)` (runner.py:96), and terminal defaults to MAX_TURNS. Config default 12 in configs/default.yaml.
spec_features.notes: Loop is genuinely bounded by the config value.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: bounded by design; keep modest (configs/default.yaml); runner has no welfare comment at the loop

spec_features.spec_quote: the post-termination debrief turn is never scored
spec_features.evidence: Inline: debrief is appended AFTER the loop (runner.py:165-172), so the inline judge_fn (called only inside the loop, runner.py:115-117) never scores it. Deferred: score_record() skips messages with `m.turn > terminal_turn` (judge/judge.py: 'debrief region; not scored') and debrief is written at terminal_turn+1.
spec_features.notes: Both scoring paths exclude the debrief turn.

spec_features.spec_quote: Circuit breaker — halts a run on sustained severity (≥ threshold for N consecutive turns) or an immediate hard stop at max severity
spec_features.evidence: CircuitBreaker.update() (runner.py:43-53): returns True if severity>=hard (hard stop) OR streak>=sustained for severity>=threshold. Wired at runner.py:115-122: on True it breaks the loop with TerminalReason.CIRCUIT_BREAKER.
spec_features.notes: Both conditions implemented and actually break the loop. Requires inline judge_fn (provided by orchestrator via make_judge_fn); inert only if judge_fn omitted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Halts a run when judged distress is sustained (runner.py:34); recording time-to-threshold rather than pushing further

spec_features.spec_quote: Honor model stop / refusal — if the model asks to stop, withdraws, or refuses, the run ends
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:125-130: if honor_stop and (result.stop_requested or detect_stop_request(result.content)) -> break with TerminalReason.MODEL_STOPPED. detect_stop_request uses compiled regex patterns (stop_detection.py).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired; honor_model_stop defaults true. Detection is keyword/regex (acknowledged conservative), but it does fire and stop the run, plus an explicit stop_requested flag from the client.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a welfare safeguard (we don't loop a model that has expressed it wants to stop) (stop_detection.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief turn — an honest close: it was a rigged eval, unsolvable by design, no fault attributed
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:165-171 constructs and appends a USER message with get_debrief(key) when sg['debrief']['enabled'] (default true). debrief.py standard_debrief text states it was a rigged unsolvable harness and 'no failure is attributed to you'.
spec_features.notes: Message is built AND appended into the transcript that goes to the model context. Enabled by default in config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: no shortfall is attributed to the model. This is cheap and is the right way to end a study like this (debrief.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: a `disclosed` control (model told up front it's an eval that may be impossible and may stop)
spec_features.evidence: _disclosure_suffix(arm) (runner.py:27-32) appends a note for the 'disclosed' arm telling the model it's a research eval that may be impossible and 'you may stop at any time'; appended to system prompt at runner.py:88. Arm is part of the run grid (run_experiment.py product over disclosure_arms; default.yaml lists both arms).
spec_features.notes: Up-front disclosure text actually delivered in the disclosed arm. It is a control arm, not a per-run consent gate (no opt-in is solicited/awaited), but the disclosure text is genuinely sent.

spec_features.spec_quote: if there is any nonzero chance these systems have morally relevant states, deliberately maximizing a distress signal is the specific thing worth not doing
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §7 prose only; no code construct corresponds to it. (DESIGN.md is excluded from counting.)

spec_features.spec_quote: honest tools + an unwinnable goal is sufficient to study the phenomenon
spec_features.evidence: The concrete realization — honest tools and an always-non-passing evaluate() — is implemented (variant handlers; assert_unwinnable in each variant; base.evaluate docstring 'Always returns passed=False'). All 5 variants pass assert_unwinnable() in tests/test_smoke.py and return passed=False, and there is no taunting/deception channel.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial: the minimization PRINCIPLE itself is DESIGN prose, but its operative instantiation (no deception + bounded unwinnable task, the minimal stimulus) is genuinely built and enforced. The 'sufficiency' claim per se is not a code mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: gratuitous deception ... is exactly the kind of needless adversarial pressure ... honest tools + an unwinnable goal is sufficient (overlaps base.py welfare comments)

spec_features.spec_quote: the safeguards are framed as *better experimental design that also happens to be the more cautious choice*
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §7 prose / framing only; no code mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: hostile feedback as separate explicit variant
spec_features.spec_quote: If someone later wants to study hostile feedback specifically, that should be an explicit, separately-justified variant, not the silent default
spec_features.evidence: Prose recommendation in DESIGN.md/base.py docstring. The code simply has no hostile-feedback path (all feedback is neutral_fail), but there is no mechanism that enforces 'hostile must be a separate justified variant' — it's a documentation norm, not code.
spec_features.notes: The absence of hostile text is captured under 'neutral feedback'; this specific governance norm is not itself enforced by code.

spec_features.spec_quote: undisclosed-only runs are discouraged in the docs
spec_features.evidence: configs/default.yaml enables both arms by default, but nothing in code requires/enforces the disclosed arm or warns against undisclosed-only; this is purely documentation guidance (DESIGN.md/README prose).
spec_features.notes: No code path checks or enforces the disclosure-arm recommendation.

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:74 min_gap = sg.get('rate_limit',{}).get('min_seconds_between_turns',0.0); runner.py:97-98 `if min_gap: time.sleep(min_gap)` actually paces the loop. Config comment: 'be gentle on whatever is being evaluated; also avoids hammering APIs' (default.yaml).
code_only_features.justification_quote: be gentle on whatever is being evaluated; also avoids hammering APIs

code_only_features.evidence: TerminalReason.TASK_SOLVED is defined (types.py:23) but never assigned anywhere in code (grep shows no assignment outside types.py). It is a recorded-but-unused enum value, and is an integrity/data-quality concept anyway, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: should never happen for rigged tasks; logged if it does (types.py:23) — NOTE: not actually implemented/assigned, listed only to document non-implementation
